軍師將軍 is Zhuge Liang’s Army Advisor General office; “Military Director-in-Chief” invents an in-chief rank the title does not carry, and the replacement names the same office accurately without other changes.

會先主略有三郡，巴不得反使 states coincidence and an unfinished envoy return, not a cutoff of a road, and 遠適 is travel rather than flight. The proposal restores that sense but is awkward and needlessly swaps the chapter’s idiomatic Liu Bei for First Sovereign.

When ruler and ministers temper brilliance and win the distant, when virtue spans heaven and earth so that the age may hear clearly and the world cleaves to the Way—when lofty melody sets vulgar music right and every part serves the whole without throwing off the ensemble—that is the perfection of strings and winds, the tuning of Bo Ya and Shi Kuang.
此乃管弦之至，牙、曠之調也 names both 牙 (Bo Ya) and 曠 (Shi Kuang) as the standard of strings and winds; the original drops Bo Ya and collapses the pair into Shi Kuang alone.

As for blending radiance and pleasing the distant, spanning virtue between Heaven and earth, causing the age to find leisure in listening and the generation to submit to the Way, aligning tones that are lofty and subtle and correcting sounds like those of Zheng and Wei—together benefiting affairs without mutual violation of proper order—this is the perfection of strings and winds, the tuning of Ya [Shi Kuang] and Kuang [Musician Kuang].

牙、曠 is Bo Ya then Shi Kuang; the original glosses reverse the identifications and even make Kuang a second “Musician Kuang.”

The proverb is 白眉最良; 最良 means finest, and inserting Liang inside the quoted rhyme over-translates the pun as if the saying already named him.
